name: Ajanta Caves
description: Carved into a 75-metre rock wall above the Waghur River gorge in Maharashtra, India, the Ajanta Caves are 30 Buddhist monasteries and worship halls cut by hand, beginning around the 2nd century BCE. Inside, vivid wall paintings retell the Buddha's past lives, and the figures convey emotion through gesture and pose. Hidden by jungle for centuries, the caves were found in 1819 by a British officer on a tiger hunt.
